g1|variants|free goods.summary: Free goods scenarios deliver materials to customers at zero sales price, either as commercial incentives linked to purchased volumes or as standalone sample and warranty shipments. Variants differ in whether the discount is determined automatically via free goods master records, generated as parent-child sub-item lines, applied directly as 100% price conditions, or governed by specialized sales document types.

variants.name: Exclusive Free Goods with Sub-Item Generation
variants.when_used: Customer orders a qualified quantity of a product and receives extra quantities of the same or different material free of charge as an additional delivery line.

OR (Standard Order)

R100 on TANN, PR00 on TAN

g1|core|free goods|exclusive free goods.title: Exclusive Free Goods with Sub-Item Generation
g1|core|free goods|exclusive free goods.story: When a customer buys ten boxes of coffee, the seller gives them an extra mug or an additional box for free. In SAP S/4HANA exclusive free goods with sub-item generation, ordering a primary product triggers the automatic creation of a distinct second line item for the promotional product at no charge. The ordered item prices normally under category TAN, while the bonus sub-item generates under category TANN, discounts to zero via condition R100, and flows through delivery and billing at 0.00 currency.
g1|core|free goods|exclusive free goods.why_business_needs_it: Trade marketing and promotional agreements require automated incentives where purchasing target volumes yields bonus units without rep-driven manual discounts. Automated sub-item generation guarantees accurate ATP inventory reservation for the gift, prints transparent line items on customer delivery slips, and issues compliant zero-value billing lines for tax and audit trails.

modules.role: Evaluates condition technique master records to determine bonus quantity and material rules during order entry.
Creates higher-level item TAN and automatically explodes dependent sub-item TANN with item usage FREE.
Picks, packs, and posts goods issue for both the main material and the free goods sub-item from inventory.
Generates commercial invoice F2 pricing the sub-item at 0.00 net value while recording tax and COGS.

g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.title: Inclusive Free Goods with Sub-Item Generation (Sales Order to Billing)
g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.story: A customer buys ten units of a product and gets two of those ten units for free, paying for only eight. In SAP S/4HANA, the sales order splits the single order line into a paid main item (TAN) for eight pieces and a free sub-item (TANN) for two pieces, delivering all ten physically while zeroing the billing price on the sub-item via condition R100.
g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.why_business_needs_it: Companies run promotional campaigns that bundle complimentary units inside the ordered quantity without increasing the total shipment volume. Inclusive sub-item generation provides full inventory trackability across warehouse fulfillment and delivers transparent invoices showing list price alongside a 100% promotional discount for customer visibility.

g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.title: Inclusive Free Goods without Sub-Item Generation (Order-to-Cash)
g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.story: A customer buys ten items, and one of those ten is free as part of an inclusive promotional deal. Instead of creating an extra free line item on the order and invoice, the system keeps the order on a single line of ten units. In SAP S/4HANA, the sales order retains item category TAN, ships the full quantity of ten physically, and calculates a proportional pricing discount condition (NR00) that subtracts the value of the free unit. The customer receives a single delivery and a single invoice line billed net for nine units.
g1|core|free goods|inclusive free goods.why_business_needs_it: High-volume consumer goods and wholesale distributors require single-line invoicing to prevent billing discrepancies and invoice rejections in customer EDI systems caused by line splits. It simplifies warehouse operations by picking against one single delivery line rather than splitting deliveries across linked main and sub-items. It also preserves clear accounting visibility by posting gross revenue alongside an explicit promotional deduction to a sales discount account.

g1|core|free goods|free-of-charge sales.title: Free-of-Charge Sales Order (Document Type FD)
g1|core|free goods|free-of-charge sales.story: A company sends free product samples or replacement items to a customer without sending an invoice. In SAP, this is handled through a dedicated sales document type that allows normal picking and warehouse dispatch, but suppresses commercial receivables while tracking inventory costs and promotional expenses.
g1|core|free goods|free-of-charge sales.why_business_needs_it: Businesses frequently provide commercial samples, marketing giveaways, and courtesy replacements without billing the customer. Using a free-of-charge order automates the bypass of customer accounts receivable while maintaining formal warehouse fulfillment, export compliance documentation, and proper Cost of Goods Sold allocation.

modules.role: Captures customer demand, validates order reasons, and generates sales order lines with zero commercial value.
Processes physical fulfillment including picking, packing, and posting goods issue for stock removal.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-GL (General Ledger) via goods issue material document posting.

modules.role: Suppresses standard commercial invoices or produces pro-forma customs invoices (F8) where international cross-border compliance applies.
Receives cost of goods sold from the goods issue to capture marketing and sample expenses by customer and product.

prerequisites: Sales Organization, Distribution Channel, Division, and Shipping Point created and assigned (SPRO / Enterprise Structure).
Customer Master / Business Partner created in the relevant Sales Area with shipping data configured (BP).
Material Master maintained with Sales, Shipping, and Plant/Storage data (MM01).
Inventory available in the issuing plant storage location (MMBE / MIGO).

g1|core|free goods|subsequent delivery f.title: Subsequent Delivery Free-of-Charge (SD with Reference)
g1|core|free goods|subsequent delivery f.story: A customer receives a damaged product or is missing items from an earlier order, so the company ships a replacement for free. Instead of typing a new order from scratch, the system copies the details directly from the original invoice or sales order so nobody enters wrong data or sends unauthorized free goods. The warehouse packs and ships the goods normally, but the finance department never sends another bill because the replacement item is configured as non-billable.
g1|core|free goods|subsequent delivery f.why_business_needs_it: It streamlines customer dispute resolutions by providing immediate replacement stock while enforcing mandatory reference checks against prior sales or billing documents. This prevents revenue leakage, ensures inventory accuracy at goods issue, and suppresses unwanted invoice generation in compliance with internal audit controls.

modules.role: Captures the subsequent free-of-charge order referencing the preceding invoice or sales order and determines the non-billable item category.
Executes delivery processing, picking, packing, and post goods issue for the replacement stock.
Deducts physical unrestricted inventory and triggers standard inventory accounting without customer receivable postings.

g1|core|free goods|line-item 100% value.title: Line-Item 100% Value Discount via Pricing
g1|core|free goods|line-item 100% value.story: Imagine a magical store where buying a giant box of crayons automatically makes one specific promotional crayon box completely free on the receipt as a price discount. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC), this means a specific pricing condition type applies a 100% value discount directly to the main sales order item, keeping the item category as TAN (Standard Item) without splitting into sub-items. The system processes the order, delivery, and billing normally, resulting in a zero net value for the discounted line item on the billing document.
g1|core|free goods|line-item 100% value.why_business_needs_it: Businesses run promotional campaigns to boost sales volume by offering 100% discounts on specific line items without altering the standard order fulfillment structure or creating separate sub-items. This maintains a clean document flow and simplifies sales reporting.

g1|panel|free goods.otc_impact: Free goods sits at the intersection of sales pricing and inventory issuance in Order-to-Cash, automatically adding promotional or bonus items to sales orders based on customer-material agreements. It alters the document flow by either splitting order lines into parent-child sub-items or discounting line items to zero, driving downstream outbound deliveries, cost of goods sold postings, and zero-dollar billings. If misconfigured, it distorts revenue recognition, inflates inventory write-offs, and breaks customer trust through incorrect invoice discrepancies.

panel_qa.question: How do we decide between inclusive free goods with sub-item generation versus a 100% pricing discount?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Inclusive free goods with sub-item generation creates a separate child line item in the sales order, which is essential for accurate inventory tracking, warehouse picking, and statutory free-sample reporting. Conversely, a 100% value discount via pricing keeps the single line item intact, avoiding document clutter and simplifying billing, but sacrifices inventory visibility for the promotional quantity. We implement sub-item generation when warehouse pick accuracy and inventory reduction of the specific bonus material are legally or operationally required. From a leadership perspective, sub-item generation protects gross margin reporting by isolating cost of goods sold for the giveaway while pricing discounts hide promotional costs within net revenue adjustments. Next, we will review our product catalog to ensure all promotional items have proper material masters for sub-item splits.
panel_qa.trap: We use pricing discounts because sub-items confuse the warehouse pickers.

panel_qa.question: What prevents sales representatives from manually overriding free goods conditions and eroding our operating margins?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: We enforce strict access sequences and pricing determination procedures in transaction V/08 where free goods conditions are marked as mandatory and non-manually changeable. Condition types like NA00 or NR00 are restricted via pricing permission groups so that sales reps cannot alter the calculated free quantity or discount percentage in transaction VA01. Financially, this control eliminates unauthorized promotional giveaways, safeguarding operating cash flow and protecting EBITDA margins from margin leakage. Operationally, it ensures consistent application of trade promotion agreements across all sales channels without relying on manual user vigilance. Next, we will audit user profile authorizations for pricing overrides to close any existing loopholes.
panel_qa.trap: We trust our sales reps to apply free goods only when customers qualify.

panel_qa.question: How does exclusive free goods integration affect our available-to-promise check and delivery scheduling?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Exclusive free goods replace the ordered material with a different bonus material as a sub-item, triggering a fresh availability check in transaction VA01 for the newly determined free material. The system executes a new availability check using checking group settings in transaction OVZ9 and requirement classes defined in transaction OVZI for the sub-item. If the bonus material lacks stock, the main item delivery block can be propagated depending on the incompletion log and schedule line configuration. This integration ensures we never promise free stock we do not physically possess, preventing warehouse fulfillment delays and backorder disputes. Next, we will align warehouse safety stock parameters with our top promotional materials to support smooth automated order fulfillment.
panel_qa.trap: Exclusive free goods automatically inherit the availability confirmation of the main paid item.

panel_qa.question: Why use a subsequent delivery free-of-charge document instead of a standard sales order with 100% pricing?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Subsequent delivery free-of-charge uses sales document type SD to handle customer compensation or warranty replacements without impacting current sales revenue or billing history. It bypasses standard pricing completely, setting pricing procedure to empty while still generating outbound deliveries and goods issues for inventory tracking. This segregation is critical for audit compliance, ensuring that goodwill replacements and quality returns are clearly separated from commercial sales volume in financial reporting. From a risk perspective, it prevents distortion of customer profitability analysis (CO-PA) by routing costs to specific quality or marketing expense accounts rather than reducing product revenue. Next, we will standardise reason-for-ordering codes to categorise the root cause of all subsequent deliveries.
panel_qa.trap: We just create standard sales orders with zero price because it uses fewer document types.

panel_qa.question: How do free goods without sub-item generation impact our statutory value-added tax and billing output?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Inclusive free goods without sub-item generation apply a 100% discount directly to the item price using condition techniques, leaving the billing quantity unchanged. In billing transaction VF01, the net value calculates to zero, but the tax determination engine (such as Vertex or TAXUSX) evaluates whether statutory tax is due on the normal list price or zero value based on local tax jurisdiction laws. Financially, this approach simplifies the invoice layout for the customer while requiring precise tax condition record maintenance to comply with regional tax authorities regarding promotional giveaways. Operationally, it reduces billing item counts, speeding up spool generation and EDI transmission times. Next, we will validate regional tax rules with our tax advisors to ensure zero-value items comply with local invoicing mandates.
panel_qa.trap: Free goods without sub-items never generate any tax liability in billing.

panel_qa.question: What is the S/4HANA cloud best practice for maintaining free goods master data efficiently at scale?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: In SAP S/4HANA, we utilize transaction V/69 for condition maintenance and leverage SAP Fiori app 'Manage Free Goods' or data migration cockpit templates to upload mass promotional agreements. Free goods master data relies on condition tables combining customer hierarchy, material pricing groups, and validity periods to minimise record redundancy. By centralising maintenance through condition records rather than hardcoding in material masters, we reduce administrative overhead and prevent outdated promotional pricing from leaking into active orders. Operationally, this ensures real-time pricing updates take effect instantly across all sales channels without system downtime. Next, we will implement workflow approvals for new free goods condition record creation.
panel_qa.trap: We manually maintain free goods conditions in every customer master record individually.
